# dspgv

> Computes all eigenvalues and, optionally, the eigenvectors of a real.

<section class="intro">

generalized symmetric-definite eigenproblem in packed storage.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dspgv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dspgv';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dspgv( order, itype, jobz, uplo, N, AP, BP, w, strideW, Z, LDZ, WORK ) → info: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `itype` | `integer` | Problem type (1, 2, or 3)<br>Rejects `itype < 1 \|\| itype > 3` |
| `jobz` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrices A and B<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `AP` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | **in/out** · Packed symmetric matrix A (length N\*(N+1)/2) |
| `BP` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | **in/out** · Packed symmetric positive definite matrix B (length N\*(N+1)/2) |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array for eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output eigenvector matrix (N x N) |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of Z<br>Rejects `ldz < 1 \|\| (jobz === 'compute-vectors' && ldz < N)` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 3 * N</sub> | **out** · Workspace array (length >= 3\*N) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `itype`: Specifies the problem type to be solved:

  -   `= 1`: $A \, x = (\lambda ) \, B \, x$
  -   `= 2`: $A \, B \, x = (\lambda ) \, x$
  -   `= 3`: $B \, A \, x = (\lambda ) \, x$
- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangles of A and B are stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangles of A and B are stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrices A and B. $N \ge 0$.
- `AP`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the symmetric matrix A, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of A is stored in the array `AP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = A(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*(2*n-j)/2) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$.

  On exit, the contents of `AP` are destroyed.
- `BP`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the symmetric matrix B, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of B is stored in the array `BP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `BP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = B(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `BP(i + (j-1)*(2*n-j)/2) = B(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$.

  On exit, the triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $B = U^T \, U$ or $B = L \, L^T$, in the same storage format as B.
- `w`: If `INFO = 0`, the eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, Z contains the matrix Z of eigenvectors. The eigenvectors are normalized as follows: if `ITYPE = 1` or 2, $Z^T \, B \, Z = I$; if `ITYPE = 3`, $Z^T \, \operatorname{inv}(B) \, Z = I$. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument is invalid (rejected when `itype < 1 \|\| itype > 3`)
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eleventh argument is invalid (rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < N )`)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dspgv.ndarray(
    itype,
    jobz, uplo,
    N,
    AP, strideAP, offsetAP,
    BP, strideBP, offsetBP,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → info: integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `itype` | `integer` | Problem type (1, 2, or 3)<br>Rejects `itype < 1 \|\| itype > 3` |
| `jobz` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrices A and B<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `AP` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | **in/out** · Packed symmetric matrix A; on exit, overwritten |
| ↳ `strideAP` | `integer` | Stride length for `AP` |
| ↳ `offsetAP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AP` |
| `BP` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | **in/out** · Packed symmetric positive definite matrix B; on exit, Cholesky factor |
| ↳ `strideBP` | `integer` | Stride length for `BP` |
| ↳ `offsetBP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `BP` |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array for eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride for `w` |
| ↳ `offsetW` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `w` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output eigenvector matrix (N x N); referenced only if jobz = `'compute-vectors'` |
| ↳ `strideZ1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `Z` |
| ↳ `strideZ2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `Z` |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `Z` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 3 * N</sub> | **out** · Workspace array (length >= 3\*N) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `itype`: Specifies the problem type to be solved:

  -   `= 1`: $A \, x = (\lambda ) \, B \, x$
  -   `= 2`: $A \, B \, x = (\lambda ) \, x$
  -   `= 3`: $B \, A \, x = (\lambda ) \, x$
- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangles of A and B are stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangles of A and B are stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrices A and B. $N \ge 0$.
- `AP`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the symmetric matrix A, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of A is stored in the array `AP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = A(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*(2*n-j)/2) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$.

  On exit, the contents of `AP` are destroyed.
- `BP`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the symmetric matrix B, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of B is stored in the array `BP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `BP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = B(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `BP(i + (j-1)*(2*n-j)/2) = B(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$.

  On exit, the triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $B = U^T \, U$ or $B = L \, L^T$, in the same storage format as B.
- `w`: If `INFO = 0`, the eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, Z contains the matrix Z of eigenvectors. The eigenvectors are normalized as follows: if `ITYPE = 1` or 2, $Z^T \, B \, Z = I$; if `ITYPE = 3`, $Z^T \, \operatorname{inv}(B) \, Z = I$. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful, >0 if dpptrf or dspev failed

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument is invalid (rejected when `itype < 1 \|\| itype > 3`)
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: DPPTRF or DSPEV returned an error code: \<= N:  if `INFO = i`, DSPEV failed to converge; i off-diagonal elements of an intermediate tridiagonal form did not converge to zero.
-   `> N`: if $\mathrm{INFO} = n + i$, for $1 \le i \le n$, then the leading principal minor of order i of B is not positive. The factorization of B could not be completed and no eigenvalues or eigenvectors were computed.

</section>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dspgv()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DSPGV`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dspgv.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dspgv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dspgv';

const AP = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 2.0, 5.0, 1.0, 3.0, 6.0 ] );
const BP = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 2.0, 5.0, 0.0, 1.0, 3.0 ] );
const W = new Float64Array( 3 );
const Z = new Float64Array( 9 );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 9 );

const info = dspgv( 'column-major', 1, 'compute-vectors', 'upper', 3, AP, BP, W, 1, Z, 3, WORK ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info );
console.log( 'Eigenvalues (W):', W );
console.log( 'Eigenvectors (Z):', Z );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DSPGV`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DSPGV computes all the eigenvalues and, optionally, the eigenvectors of a real generalized symmetric-definite eigenproblem, of the form $A \, x=(\lambda ) \, B \, x$, $A \, \mathrm{Bx}=(\lambda ) \, x$, or $B \, A \, x=(\lambda ) \, x$. Here A and B are assumed to be symmetric, stored in packed format, and B is also positive definite.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
